attempts.name: cockpit-1
attempts.prompt: Photoreal interior of a generic modern electric car at night, seen perfectly straight-on and symmetric, camera centred and level with the dashboard. A long dark dashboard spans the image. On it sit two switched-off screens, each a flat matte black rectangle with a thin dark bezel and sharp square corners, facing the camera exactly head-on with no perspective: a large wide 16:9 central display in the middle-left, and to its right a separate tall portrait passenger display about two-thirds as wide as it is tall, the same height as the central display. Only the top arc of the steering wheel rim is visible at the far left edge. A thin soft violet-blue ambient light strip runs along the dashboard below the screens. Dark leather and brushed metal, city lights blurred through the windshield. No brand, no logos, no text, no badges, no reflections on the screens.
attempts.verdict: straight-on and convincing, but the screens span only ~62% of the width: the largest 16:9 driver fit would be ~1040 px wide on the 1920 canvas, 80% of the procedural layout, and the driver screen (2.17:1 merged region) is not a clean 16:9 window

attempts.name: cockpit-2
attempts.prompt: Front elevation of a minimalist concept car dashboard at night, orthographic, perfectly flat and symmetric, like a product design render. Two large blank screens are mounted flush on the dashboard: a wide landscape 16:9 screen and, to its right, a tall portrait screen with a 2:3 aspect ratio. Both screens are pure flat matte black rectangles with thin even bezels and crisp straight edges, perfectly axis-aligned, no glare, no content. The two screens together fill most of the image width. Part of a steering wheel rim curves in from the lower left corner. A glowing indigo ambient light line traces the dashboard under the screens, soft rim light on dark materials. Generic, no brand, no logos, no text.
attempts.verdict: large screens, but the wide one is 1.47:1, not 16:9, and the steering wheel crosses its lower-left corner, so a recording cannot sit in it unoccluded

attempts.name: graffiti-2
attempts.prompt: Cinematic wide photograph of a New York City subway car parked in a dim station at night. Its brushed stainless-steel side carries one bold, perfectly legible wildstyle graffiti piece that spells exactly "Muse2CarUI", painted in electric purple, cobalt blue and amber spray paint with glowing highlights and paint drips; the letters are filled with subtle car-dashboard gauges and circuit-trace motifs. The lettering is centred horizontally and sits slightly above the middle of the frame, with darker empty steel below it. Wet platform reflections, moody teal and violet light. Photoreal. No other words, no logos, no brand names, no people.
attempts.verdict: legible but smaller lettering than graffiti-1 and graffiti-3
